newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Arjo Wiggins feels worst days over.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Arjo Wiggins feels worst days over.

text.p: British paper and packaging group Arjo Wiggins Appleton Plc said on Thursday it hoped to cut its European costs by another 30 million pounds ($48.4 million) in 1997.
"The management's actions are bearing fruit...we think we have left our worst days behind," Arjo Wiggins' chief executive Phillippe Beylier told Reuters.
Beylier, who was elevated to the post on Wednesday after the resignation of Daniel Melin, was speaking shortly after the group posted an annual pre-tax profit of 133.9 million pounds for 1996.
Beylier said the group was able reduce costs by eight million pounds in 1996 and hopes to reduce it by another 30 million in 1997.
"The conditions are favourable for us," he said.
The group's turnover rose slightly to 3.57 billion pounds from 3.56 billion and maintained its dividend at 7.5 pence per share.
The group has recently been hit by a decline in pulp prices which led to an overall weakening of the industry and put pressure on margins.
Beylier said he expected pulp prices to weaken slightly, around five to six percent, but did not expect this to hamper the company's businesses further.
The company's restructuring programme was ahead of schedule in Europe, its main market, where its carbonless and thermal businesses were recovering volumes and returning close to break-even levels.
The group's European coated paper business remained difficult, but it was able to convert a small loss in the first half to mild profits in the second by improving productivity per employee.
Beylier said the management was going through each of its businesses to achive the lowest possible headcount.
He said the group faced no need to reduce workforce in the UK but might have to do so in Europe. Beylier declined to mention any numbers.
